To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

phagosomal group B streptoccus (GBS) but not cytosol bacteria potently induced interferons in conventional DC by a mechanism that requires TLR7, MyD88 and IRF1, and that all three proteins localized together with GBS in degradative phagosomal vacuoles bearing LAMP-1 and Cathepsins.
phagosomal RNA induces interferon in conventional DCs by a mechanism requiring the TLR7-MyD88-IRF1 pathway, which is located in the lysosomes.

phagosomal group B streptcoccus (but not cytosolic) bacteria potently induced interferons by a TLR7-dependent mechanism, which was mediated by lysosomal localization of TLR7, the adaptor protein MyD88, and the transcription factor interferon regulatory factor 1 (IRF1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recognition of bacterial pathogens by cells of the innate immune system, and the consequences of this recognition.
the molecular mechanisms of innate immune responses to microbial pathogens and the regulation of these responses by the host cell.
the mechanisms that control how cells respond to infection by pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lysosome is the organelle where TLR7 recognizes bacterial RNA, and the lysosome is also the organelle that is required for the induction of type 1 interferon.
TLR7 recognizes bacterial RNA in lysosomes of conventional DCs, but not of plasmacytoid DCs.
the lysosome is an important site of innate immune recognition and that the type of recognition is dictated by the subcellulate location of the receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TLR7 is a lysosomal receptor that is used by conventional dendritic cells to detect bacterial RNA.
the recognition of group B streptcoccus (GBS) RNA by TLR7 is mediated in conventional dendritic (cDC) cells via the MyD88-dependent signaling pathway.
TLR7 recognizes bacterial RNA in the lysosome of conventional dendritic cell to trigger the production of interferon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lysosome-associated Toll-like receptors can be used to detect bacterial RNA in the context of conventional dendritic cell activation.
the subcellular site where bacteria are encountered can determine the type of innate immune response that ensues.
lysosomal TLR7 is the key receptor for sensing bacterial RNA and that this sensing is required to activate type 1 interferon responses in conventional dendritic cell (cDC).
